A sudden cooling of the Northern Hemisphere that began in 536, one of the worst in the last two thousand years. A volcanic eruption, perhaps more than one, threw a veil of fine particles into the sky. In Constantinople Procopius wrote that for a whole year the sun gave light without brightness, like the moon.

Summers in Europe were as much as 2.5 °C colder than normal. Tree rings show stunted growth across the world, and writers in Italy, Ireland and China recorded failed harvests and famine. The source volcano is unknown. Further eruptions around 540 and 547 kept the cold going, and scientists speak of a Late Antique Little Ice Age lasting until about 660.

Within five years the Plague of Justinian broke out. Some historians think hunger and cold helped it spread, and that together they weakened the eastern empire just as Justinian was fighting to win back the west.
